results_section: 1. At the longest context length (4096 tokens), ATSKV requires only 8.1 MB of memory compared to 41.1 MB for the full cache, representing an 80.3% reduction in memory usage.
2. In the Longbench benchmark (Figure 1), the gap between ATSKV and the full cache widens from 3.9 MB at 512 tokens to 33.0 MB at 4096 tokens.
3. ATSKV achieves an average of 15% lower memory usage compared to RocketKV, the second-best method, across all benchmarks and context lengths.
4. At 4096 tokens, ATSKV reduces the time to first token by approximately 20% compared to the full cache baseline and by 18% compared to DynamicKV.

5. ATSKV consistently achieves the highest throughput across all benchmarks and context lengths, with up to 23.6 tokens per second at 512 tokens, compared to 19.5 tokens per second for the full cache baseline, representing a 21% improvement in generation speed.
6. Even at 4096 tokens, ATSKV maintains a 19% throughput advantage over the full cache baseline.
7. ATSKV maintains accuracy within 1% of the full cache baseline across all benchmarks and context lengths.
8. At 4096 tokens, ATSKV achieves 48.3% accuracy on Longbench compared to 48.9% for the full cache, representing only a 0.6 percentage point difference.
9. At 4096 tokens, the sliding window approach achieves only 41.8% accuracy on Longbench, 7.1 percentage points lower than the full cache baseline.
10. Removing the attention-derived features (a_i^l) from the relevance predictor resulted in a 2.1 percentage point drop in accuracy.
11. Removing the handcrafted features (f_i^l) resulted in a 1.3 percentage point drop in accuracy.
12. At 90% sparsity (retaining only 10% of tokens), accuracy dropped by 3.7 percentage points compared to the full cache baseline.
13. Disabling the external memory integration resulted in a 1.2 percentage point drop in accuracy for very long contexts (4096 tokens).
14. The dynamic threshold adaptation strategy improved accuracy by 1.8 percentage points compared to fixed thresholds, particularly for variable-length contexts.
